prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (RDC, call sign Juniper) provides 24/7 emergency medical call intake, controlled triage-support process, ambulance dispatch, regional coordination/shared operational picture. Mandate: convert reported emergencies into prioritized incident records and coordinate response under approved clinical/jurisdictional protocols; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy. RDC compares reported conditions with current zone coverage, escalates unresolved readiness gaps, and reassesses readiness after significant incidents/service interruptions/route-access changes.
Elements/actors: Call Taker Mara (radio alias Larkspur) establishes caller location before medical details; asks street address, municipality, building/floor/entrance; confirms by repeat-back/landmarks; asks callback; collects patient age, consciousness, breathing, chief reason, symptom onset if reliable; distinguishes observed vs hearsay symptoms; notes access barriers; remains engaged if info may change priority/access plan. Mara enters request/incident via Computer Aided Dispatch Console (CAD Console), which checks address/map data and supports dispatch; staff must verify displayed currency. If location unresolved Mara asks focused follow-ups/updates record; produces Caller Location Correction Slip for documented address clarification.
Triage Supervisor reviews incident information, assigns/confirms priority, directs/coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch when demand/access changes. Regional Medical Director owns clinical triage policy/limits. Shift Commander (Sundial) is on-duty operational authority for coordination, service continuity, surge priorities, conflict resolution, jurisdictional escalation, and readiness concerns needing repositioning/local coverage adjustment; must not replace Medical Director authority or Paramedic Crew scene judgment. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network/channels/backups/radio checks. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) monitors serviceability, servicing, defects, availability; produces Battery Swap Voucher. Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel) coordinates receiving capacity/destination constraints; Emergency Department sends receiving considerations; Riverside Trauma Center designated destination. Paramedic Crew assesses/cares for patient and reports access barriers/vehicle readiness concerns via established communications. Ambulance Unit 417 may be assigned.
Ambulance Coordination Platform maintains incidents, assignments, resource status and shared view of zone coverage/unit availability. Response zones have maintained boundaries and primary/alternate routes to ED/Riverside; crews verify changing access. North/South Gate Status Boards provide access/restriction/queue info; North produces North Approach Queue Snapshot.

New part:
S066: The Hospital Liaison Desk supports intake coordination by confirming facility capabilities and clarifying hospital contact pathways.
S067: The Hospital Liaison Desk checks whether a reported destination preference is compatible with current facility capabilities.
S068: When a facility constraint affects coordination, the Hospital Liaison Desk records the constraint in the incident notes.
S069: The Hospital Liaison Desk produces the Bedside Arrival Receipt when an ambulance arrival has been confirmed.
S070: The Hospital Liaison Desk provides current facility information through established coordination channels without delaying emergency call intake.
S071: The Triage Supervisor reviews incidents when the reported symptoms or uncertainty warrant clinical escalation.
S072: The Data Quality Officer monitors intake records for recurring gaps in location or medical detail.
S073: Call Taker Mara updates the incident record when a caller provides new information before dispatch decisions are finalized.
S074: The Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S075: Clinical triage begins after Call Taker Mara has captured the caller's reported symptoms, location, and immediate hazards.
S076: The recorded information provides an initial basis for assigning urgency and does not replace clinical reassessment as new information arrives.
S077: Triage Supervisor reviews incidents with uncertain severity, conflicting reports, or signs of rapid deterioration.
S078: Priority is based on the immediacy of threat to life, the likely time sensitivity of care, and the risk of deterioration while awaiting response.
S079: Incidents indicating an immediate threat receive the highest available response priority and prompt dispatch action.
S080: Incidents without an immediate threat are prioritized according to the expected harm from delay and the patient's reported condition.
S081: When essential information is missing, Triage Supervisor directs focused clarification while ensuring that information gathering does not delay an urgent response.
S082: Triage Supervisor escalates clinically ambiguous or unusually severe cases to Regional Medical Director for guidance when time permits.
S083: Regional Medical Director provides clinical policy guidance and does not replace the operational authority responsible for dispatch decisions.
S084: Triage Supervisor sends the Pediatric Acuity Note.
S085: Triage Supervisor is known operationally as Copperfield.
S086: Data Quality Officer is known operationally as Pebble.
S087: Data Quality Officer monitors incident records for missing, inconsistent, or duplicated information that could impair triage or dispatch.
S088: Data Quality Officer sends the Duplicate Incident Audit Memo.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
